pitch_detail.notes: Shared with Let it Burn and the West Face. A few steep moves up the broken ramp system trending right, past a tree, then easier ground to a flat ledge below a vertical splitter. Grades given for this pitch range from 5.7 to 5.8.
A short thin-hands splitter, roughly 25 ft of hard climbing, then easier ground up and left along the ledge to the trees at its far left end for the belay.

Finger cracks lead to a V-slot with a thin crack. The flakes on the left are detached: step on them rather than pull. Go up and right past a small roof, then traverse left past two bolts on the crux moves. Finish on knobs and a finger crack to a two-bolt belay. The old fixed pin is gone and leaves a good cam placement.
Hands and fingers on knobs, fins and thin cracks, stepping right twice into new crack systems, to a double crack. Belay at a fixed pin and a bolt on a small ledge.

Move into the right-slanting flared slot, mantle right onto a square ledge, then make a powerful layback past an overhanging flake. Near the top of this pitch Accendo Lunae leaves Let it Burn: belay on a bench to the right, on gear around 1 in.

New terrain. Traverse right, then climb a gently overhanging line of thin cracks and tips locks. The crux passes a wedged flake that flexes, so gear placements beside it are unreliable. Belay in a small alcove in the chimney just right of a razor-sharp flake. Grades for this pitch range from 5.11c to 5.12-.

New terrain. Awkward body positions up a tips crack in a V-shaped flare lead to a stance under a 4 ft roof where the corner switches from right-facing to left-facing. Good gear overhead protects a double hand-jam pull over the roof into thin hands, which fights up to a ledge. Grades given run from 5.11- to mid-5.11.

Back on the West Face for its crux: a perfect hand crack up the arching corner to an even bigger roof, surmounted on its left side to a stance. Grades range from 5.11+ to 5.12-; the first ascensionist rated it closer to 5.11c.

The West Face's overhanging chimneys. Fight past the first overhang into a squeeze chimney, exit to a crack, then into a second flaring chimney. Step right at a big block to belay on a large ledge. Originally rated 5.8, it is widely regarded as climbing like 5.10.

Easy blocky ground up and right to the summit, usually simul-climbed. A notch on the far right gives quick access to the walk-off. From the summit block a single 30 m rappel east off a slung horn reaches the descent.
